summary: Iteration 3 full-stack verification of the HOMENETMEN HASK platform. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_archive_profile_iter3.py (24 new cases) covering archived-exclusion on public endpoints, /api/members archive filters, /chapters/{id} active-leaders filter, PUT /users/{uid}/public-profile national_admin-only authz (403 for chapter_admin / self / scout / anon, 404 for unknown uid), split scout/leader registration + approval materialization, and galleries multi-image upload with /public/galleries 12-image trimming. Full suite now 109/109 PASS. Frontend: verified Guest homepage clickable leader cards -> leader-dialog for anonymous, chapter_admin and national_admin; edit trigger correctly hidden for anonymous and for ALL 6 leader cards when logged in as chapter_admin (including their own card), visible only for national_admin; edited position/bio/phone via leader-form-save and confirmed persistence on the card and in the dialog after a hard reload. Also exercised Members page archive toggle, Trash Bin, Administration users/pending tabs and Galleries page. All 17 requested review items PASS. Found 1 HIGH product gap (archived members are unrecoverable) plus data-integrity and asset issues detailed below.

critical.issue: DELETE /api/members/{id} soft-archives a member (status='archived'), but there is NO unarchive/restore endpoint for members and GET /api/trash only returns chapters, badges and resources. Archived members are therefore permanently unrecoverable through the API. Reproduced live: all 35 seeded members were sitting in status='archived' (Members page and public stats showed 0 members) and could only be recovered with a direct MongoDB script. Add POST /api/members/{id}/unarchive and include members in /api/trash + a Members tab in Trash.jsx.

minor.issue: Hard-deletes the chapter document without cascading/reassigning its members. 7 members are still pointing at the deleted chapter 'chp_tavush', so the Members table renders the raw id 'chp_tavush' in the Chapter column. Either block delete when members exist or archive instead of delete.
Does not exclude archived items — archived chapters/badges/members are still returned by global search, which contradicts requirement 3 ('archived items must not appear in default lists').

Non-idempotent (early-returns when any national_admin exists). All three seeded leader accounts (ararat.leader / sevan.leader / gyumri.leader) were missing from the users collection again this iteration, so every leader login returned 401 until they were re-created by a script. Make seed() upsert each documented account so /app/memory/test_credentials.md stays valid.
No role/chapter scoping — any authenticated user (including scout) receives every gallery from every chapter, while POST/DELETE are leader-scoped. Inconsistent authorization.

ui_bugs.issue: Broken image rendered on the PUBLIC homepage and on /galleries: gallery 'Summer Camp 2026' has cover = 'data:image/png;base64,AAA=' (invalid base64) and 0 images, so the browser shows the broken-image glyph. Add an onError fallback/placeholder for gallery covers and validate uploaded base64 on the server.
Trash Bin only exposes tabs Chapters / Badges / Resources. No Members tab, so archived members cannot be restored from the UI (matches the backend gap above).

Header always renders the 'Sign in' CTA (data-testid=guest-signin-btn) even when the visitor is authenticated (verified as national_admin). Should switch to 'Dashboard'/account menu when user is present.

issues: Radix DialogContent is missing a Description / aria-describedby — logs 'Warning: Missing `Description` or `aria-describedby={undefined}` for {DialogContent}' on every open (a11y).
Chapter column falls back to the raw chapter_id (e.g. 'chp_tavush') when the chapter no longer exists — show 'Unassigned' instead.
Pre-existing Recharts 'width(-1) height(-1)' console warning on first render (cosmetic).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 1845 lines — well past the 700-line threshold; split into routers (auth, chapters, members, badges, programs, galleries, admin).

Archive semantics are inconsistent: chapters/badges/resources use an `archived: true` boolean while users/members overload `status: 'archived'`. Only the boolean-based entities got unarchive endpoints and Trash coverage, which is exactly why members became unrecoverable. Unify on one convention.
DELETE /api/members/{id} performs an archive, not a delete — misleading verb/semantics for API consumers; consider POST /members/{id}/archive.

PUT /users/{uid}/public-profile correctly uses require_roles('national_admin') and returns a projection without password_hash/_id — verified 403 for chapter_admin, self and scout, 401/403 for anonymous, 404 for unknown uid.

approve_user inserts `prof` (a dict lifted from the target user document) via insert_one; the response is {'ok': True} so no ObjectId leaks today, but the same mutate-then-return risk from iteration 1 applies if this ever returns the doc.
GET /api/galleries ignores the caller's role/chapter while POST/DELETE enforce it — tighten for consistency.

rca_of_the_issue: 1) Archived members unrecoverable: the archive system was implemented twice with different shapes — chapters/badges/resources use `archived: true` and each got an /unarchive endpoint plus a /api/trash bucket, while users and members instead overload `status`. Users got POST /users/{uid}/unarchive (surfaced via Administration's SHOW ARCHIVED toggle) but members got neither an unarchive route nor a /api/trash bucket nor a Trash.jsx tab, so DELETE /api/members/{id} is a one-way door. Repro: DELETE /api/members/{id} then GET /api/trash -> member absent, and no route exists to reset status. 2) Leader logins 401: seed() returns early whenever a national_admin exists, so any seeded account removed from the DB is never recreated; the three leader accounts were absent again this iteration. Mitigation applied: direct-DB restore scripts under /app/backend/tests/. 3) Broken public image: an invalid base64 cover ('data:image/png;base64,AAA=') was accepted by POST /api/galleries and there is no onError fallback on the , so the broken-image glyph renders on the guest landing page.
